intro: Convolution can be represented as matrix multiplication after gathering local windows. Make the window order explicit.
task: Extract valid image patches as flattened rows and return their top-left coordinates.
requirements: image is a single-channel height-by-width matrix. kernel_size and stride are two-entry integer vectors in 1..64. The kernel must fit the image.

Use no padding. Visit top-left positions row first, then column, stepping by stride. Flatten each patch in row-major order. Return {"patches": matrix, "positions": integer matrix with [row,column] per patch}.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Full image patch
examples.output:
{'patches': [[1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]], 'positions': [[0, 0]]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Pointwise patches

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: A valid top-left coordinate leaves the entire kernel inside the image.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Row-major flattening visits adjacent columns before the next patch row.

explanation: The patch matrix makes local receptive fields explicit. Multiplying its rows by flattened kernel weights produces the corresponding valid convolution outputs.
Overlapping patches duplicate image values in this representation. That duplication can increase memory use even though a direct convolution could reuse the original pixels.
